title: GatherSlot: Saturday pickup shifts (fictional simulation)
targetCustomer: Mira, a fictional neighborhood food-swap volunteer coordinator
problem: Fill three Saturday pickup shifts without double-booking a volunteer
valueProposition: GatherSlot proposes one-screen assignment with an availability check
criticalTask: Assign three pickup shifts and identify overlapping assignments before publishing
verdictRationale: In these invented notes, two direct options handle signup and one checks overlaps, while the quicker options leave conflict checking to the coordinator. This is only a simulation.

topThreat.name: RosterCove
topThreat.why: Its simulated conflict warning meets the most important task requirement; setup friction remains.

opportunity.label: Fast conflict-safe assignment
opportunity.evidence: The invented RosterCove flow checks overlaps but takes several setup screens; the invented faster flows do not check them.

recommendation.nextTest: Ask five real coordinators to assign three shifts in a prototype and observe errors and setup time before making a product decision.

competitors.name: ShiftBerry
competitors.whyCompetes: Offers pickup-slot signup to the same fictional coordinator.
competitors.valueProposition: Share a volunteer signup link quickly.
competitors.businessModel: Fictional free basic tier; paid reminders.
competitors.taskSteps: Create slots; send link; volunteers select slots; review roster.
competitors.taskOutcome: Slots can be filled, but overlaps are not flagged.
competitors.strength: Invented flow makes signup links easy to share.
competitors.friction: Coordinator must check overlapping shifts separately.
competitors.advantages: Fast link sharing; low initial cost.
competitors.replicability: Both appear easy to replicate in this simulation.
competitors.customerEvidence: Two invented positive comments about link sharing; one invented conflict complaint. These are not real reviews.
competitors.swotThreats: A faster conflict-safe option could displace it.
competitors.evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comments are invented

competitors.name: RosterCove
competitors.whyCompetes: Offers scheduling and overlap checks to the same fictional coordinator.
competitors.valueProposition: Plan recurring volunteer shifts with conflict warnings.
competitors.taskEntry: Coordinator creates an account and recurring schedule.
competitors.taskSteps: Set recurrence; import availability; assign people; resolve flagged overlap; publish.
competitors.taskOutcome: Overlapping assignments are flagged before publication.
competitors.strength: Invented flow catches the target error.
competitors.friction: Several setup screens and an account for a small event.
competitors.replicability: Conflict logic appears replicable; recurring workflow takes more work.
competitors.customerEvidence: Two invented positive comments about warnings; one invented setup complaint. These are not real reviews.
competitors.swotThreats: A lighter tool with the same warning could displace it.
competitors.evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comments are invented

competitors.name: PatchPad
competitors.whyCompetes: A generic shared table can hold the same three pickup slots.
competitors.valueProposition: Let a small group edit a shared table.
competitors.taskSteps: Make rows; share edit access; volunteers add names; manually inspect conflicts.
competitors.taskOutcome: Assignments are visible; overlap checking is manual.
competitors.strength: Flexible, low-effort setup in the invented flow.
competitors.replicability: Generic table is easy to imitate but its familiarity may be hard to displace.
competitors.customerEvidence: One invented positive comment only; it is an anecdote, not a pattern.
competitors.swotThreats: Purpose-built tools could reduce coordinator effort.
competitors.evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comment is invented

competitors.name: Paper board
competitors.whyCompetes: A coordinator can fill slots by asking volunteers on site.
competitors.valueProposition: List available shifts without a device or account.
competitors.businessModel: No software charge; coordinator time is required.
competitors.taskEntry: Coordinator posts a board at the swap.
competitors.taskSteps: Write slots; collect names; remember or manually verify conflicts.
competitors.taskOutcome: On-site names are recorded; remote volunteers cannot see current assignments.
competitors.friction: Remote visibility and conflict checking are weak.
competitors.advantages: Zero software cost; visible on site.
competitors.replicability: Trivial to copy; no durable technical advantage.
competitors.customerEvidence: One invented missed-shift comment only; it is an anecdote, not a pattern.
competitors.swotWeaknesses: No remote access or automatic warning.
competitors.swotOpportunities: Could combine with a phone photo or message.
competitors.evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comment is invented
